text:
maya: heads-up — after flipping the slab handoff + int8-kv path on the m-ix hosts I see an uptick in p95 decode latency and a small quality drift on long sequences. posting quick findings and a couple offsets i captured.

jonah: ah ok, which workload/sched? smallburst or steady throughput?

maya: mostly steady throughput 50rps model=xl-8k, batch target 8, slab handoff enabled at 30% memory pressure. reproduces locally with the microbench harness.

lee: can you paste the perf run? curious about kernel selection flips.

maya: here — run script used: ```./bench_decode --model xl-8k --kv-precision int8 --slab-handoff=on --batch-target=8 --seq=1536 --iters=200```

maya: p95 numbers cropped from perf log: ```
# baseline (fp8-kv): p50 24ms, p95 48ms, mem_kv=3.2GB
# int8-kv + slab handoff: p50 22ms, p95 58ms, mem_kv=1.9GB
# int8-kv no handoff: p50 23ms, p95 50ms, mem_kv=2.0GB
```

rachel: interesting — p50 slightly better but p95 regressed ~20% vs fp8. suggests occasional slow path (cache miss/handoff). quality drift?

maya: yes, ran eval on 200-long prompts: rouge-drop ~0.7 for int8-kv vs fp8 on multi-turn summaries (more visible when sequence length > 1k). suspect quantization->handshake with kernel selection causing extra decode retries or longer kernel.

jonah: do we see kernel handover logs in trace? kernel selection can switch to a generic fallback if sequence length or kv-layout mismatches. those fallbacks are expensive.

maya: grabbed a sample trace when p95 spike happened: ```
[trace] select_kernel: fp8_matmul_opt -> chosen int8_matmul_fast
[trace] kv_lookup: slab_hit=false -> trigger_handoff
[trace] handoff: migrate_page 8MB -> pause 6.2ms
[trace] kernel_switch: int8_matmul_fast -> generic_matmul -> extra_copy 4.1ms
```

lee: that pause+extra_copy explains the tail. slab handoff currently does synchronous migration, which blocks decode. we should consider async prefetch or non-blocking copy for small pages.

rachel: also calibration: we calibrated int8-kv using mean/scale per-slab but not per-head quant stats. maybe occasional overflow/clamping forces fallback to higher-precision path?

maya: i ran a targeted test toggling "aggressive_calib": ```
# agressive_calib=false -> p95 58ms
# agressive_calib=true  -> p95 52ms (but mem_kv +100MB)
```

jonah: so more conservative quant improves latency but increases memory. tradeoff. what about batching heuristics? handoff tends to correlate with big batches that cause page churn.

maya: right — at burst sizes > 16 we see handoff frequency jump. suggestion: make slab handoff threshold adaptive to batch size and current batch latency SLO. small batches -> avoid handoff until steady.

lee: quick mitigation: set slab_handoff_max_copy_ms=2 and enable async_migrate for pages < 1MB. cheap to toggle in canary.

perf-bot: deploy-note: canary toggle proposed for m-ix hosts: async_migrate=true, slab_handoff_max_copy_ms=2, aggressive_calib=true. will run 2h smoke.

rachel: when canary completes, we should collect: p50/p95, kv mem footprint, and eval set quality (same 200 prompts). if q drop persists, revert int8-kv for long sequences and keep int8 for short.

jonah: also add kernel-selection telemetry to batch trace, include reason codes for fallback. want to see if clamping/overflow is triggering kernel change.

maya: i'll spin the canary and post results here. for followups: 1) async migrate experiment, 2) adaptive handoff threshold by batch size, 3) per-head int8 calibration sweep.

lee: sounds good. for the per-head sweep, i can produce a script that computes per-head min/max and per-slab hist and auto-selects scale; may reduce fallbacks.

rachel: ack. thanks for the quick triage @maya — please tag me when canary data is in. :thumbsup:
